topic.name: Finding the Nth Term of an Arithmetic Sequence Given Two Terms

question.text: The third and fourth terms of an arithmetic sequence are $-60$ and $-76,$ respectively. Determine the formula for the $n$th term of the sequence.
question.explanation:
The formula for the $n$th term is given by

\[ a_n = a_1 + (n-1)d, \]

so we need to figure out the first term $a_1$ and the common difference $d.$

Since the terms $a_3=-60$ and $a_4=-76$ are consecutive, we can subtract to find the common difference:

\begin{align*} d &= a_4-a_3 \\[3pt] &=-76-(-60) \\[3pt] &= -16 \end{align*}

Now, we can use one of our known values, say, $a_3=-60,$ to determine the first term of the sequence. Since $a_3$ is $2$ jumps after $a_1,$ we have:

\[ \eqalign{ a_3 &= a_1 + 2d \\[3pt] -60 &= a_1 + 2(-16) \\[3pt] -60 &= a_1 - 32 \\[3pt] -28 &= a_1 } \]

So the formula for the $n$th term of this arithmetic sequence is:

\[ \eqalign{ a_n&= a_{1}+(n-1)d \\[3pt] & = -28 + (n-1) (-16) \\[3pt] & = -28 - 16n + 16 \\[3pt] & = -16n - 12 } \]

example.title: Finding the Nth Term Given Two Non-Consecutive Terms

question.text: An arithmetic sequence has the $3$rd term $a_{3}=-9$ and the $8$th term $a_{8}=-19.$ Calculate the $11$th term.
question.explanation:
The formula for the $n$th term is given by

\[ a_n = a_1 + (n-1)d, \]

so we need to figure out the first term $a_1$ and the common difference $d.$

To find the common difference, we can find the total difference between the terms $a_{3}=-9$ and $a_{8}=-19$ and divide it by the number of jumps, as follows:

\begin{align*} d &= \dfrac{a_{8} -a_{3}}{8-3} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {-19-(-9)}{8-3} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {-10}{5} \\[5pt] &= -2 \end{align*}

Now, we can use one of our known values, say, $a_{3}=-9,$ to determine the first term of the sequence. Since $a_{3}$ is $2$ jumps after $a_1,$ we have:

\begin{align*} a_{3} &= a_1 + 2d \\[3pt] -9 &= a_1 + 2 (-2) \\[3pt] -9 &= a_1 - 4 \\[3pt] a_1 &= -5 \end{align*}

So, the formula for the $n$th term is:

\begin{align*} a_n &= -5 + (n-1)\cdot(-2)\\[5pt] &= -5-2n+2\\[5pt] &= -3-2n \end{align*}

Finally, we can find the $11$th term by substituting $n=11$ into the above:

\begin{align*} a_{11} &= -3-2(11) \\[3pt] &= -3-22 \\[3pt] &= -25 \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Nth Term Given Two Non-Consecutive Terms

question.text: The $7$th and $8$th terms of an arithmetic sequence are $-39$ and $-31,$ respectively. Determine the formula for the $n$th term of the sequence.
question.explanation:
The formula for the $n$th term is given by \[ a_n = a_1 + (n-1)d, \] so we need to figure out the first term $a_1$ and the common difference $d.$

Since the terms $a_{7} = -39$ and $a_{8} = -31$ are consecutive, we can subtract them to find the common difference: \begin{align*} d & = a_{8} - a_{7}\\[5pt] & = -31 - (-39)\\[5pt] & = -31 + 39\\[5pt] & = 8 \end{align*}

Now, we can use one of our known values, say, $a_{7} = -39,$ to determine the first term of the sequence. Since $a_{7}$ is $6$ jumps after $a_1,$ we have \begin{align*} a_{7} & = a_1 + 6d \\[5pt] -39 & = a_1 + 6(8) \\[5pt] -39 & = a_1 + 48 \\[5pt] -39 - 48 & = a_1\\[5pt] a_1 & = -87. \end{align*}

So, the formula for the $n$th term of this arithmetic sequence is \begin{align*} a_n & = a_{1} + (n-1)d \\[5pt] & = -87 + (n-1)(8) \\[5pt] & = -87 + 8n - 8\\[5pt] & = 8n - 95. \end{align*}
